video_directives: The main character is a static cutout: identical smile, arms-at-sides pose across all ~43s with only a tiny bob — add blinking, weight shifts, arm gestures, and reactions to each beat (shock at SOLD, relief at PAID IN FULL).
Scene cadence is decent but the 16-24s stretch lingers on near-identical crowd frames — tighten those holds and let the SOLD-tag march play faster to restore momentum.
Transitions breathe (push-ins, panning group reveals) — keep that, but add a stronger return-to-hook composition at the end so the loop back to the $1 price tag lands as a punch.

top3_directives: Brighten the header text — the muted gray fill on a dark plum sky loses punch on a small daylight screen; push it to warm white with a tighter drop shadow
The '$50,000' tag is too small and half-swallowed by the background building — enlarge it and add a stronger outline so the price contrast with '$1' reads instantly
Middle-right skyline has a soft dead zone between the sun and the $50k figure — add a midground silhouette or light detail to keep the eye path continuous
Reframe the '$9,000,000' tag — it's cut by the left frame edge and half-buried behind the '$1' badge; pull it fully inside frame with breathing room
Pull the '$12,000' tag off the right edge crop and stagger the three price tags so they don't visually collide ($4,000 and $12,000 overlap awkwardly)
Fill the dead top-third: the empty purple sky above the focal figure reads as a dead zone on a 6-inch phone — either crop tighter or add subtle atmospheric layering
Give the tilted sign a subtle drop shadow or rim light on its lower edge so it feels mounted in the scene rather than pasted on
The character's second arm is fully occluded making the silhouette read as one-armed at a glance — show a hint of the far arm or hand
Lower third is empty dark sidewalk with faint dashes; add a faint reflection of the character's glow on the wet ground to anchor the figure and use the dead zone
Resolve the $1 tag collision with the 'I'M THE PRICE' header — the center tag overlaps the moon and reads as a second caption system; keep price tags diegetic and smaller
Faded background characters on the right edge are half-cropped and muddy — either silhouette them fully or push contrast so they don't read as rendering artifacts
Add a subtle rim-light or drop shadow under the left sad character to anchor it to the ground plane like the hero figure
Fill or reduce the empty lower-third dark pavement — crop character slightly lower or add subtle ground detail/shadow texture to avoid a dead zone
The two background $1 signs are nearly identical in tone to each other — differentiate slightly or deepen the depth dimming so the hero $1 reads unmistakably first
Character's coat/door plane merges visually with the dark building behind the right shoulder — add a thin rim-light or slightly lift background brightness there for cleaner separation
Add a subtle drop shadow or outline to the $1 badge so it separates cleanly from the purple sky and doesn't visually merge with the character's hood
The $2,000 tag on the left is clipped by frame edge and crowds the smiling character — pull it right or shrink for breathing room
Slightly reduce the orange glow spill on the side characters so the center figure remains the unambiguous hero at a glance
Merge the four overlapping price tags into one clean system — '$12,000', '$8,000', '$2,000' and '$1' currently clutter the mid-band and tag edges are cropped at the frame
Fill the large empty top 40% (dark sky/moon) — the frame has a big dead zone above the characters; raise subjects or add subtle depth elements
Add one unmistakable focal point — the $1 character reads as subject but the hat figure competes at equal size/glow; dim one side to guide the eye
Brighten the muted gray-blue city buildings and street — they currently sit only ~10% above the background, muddying foreground separation on small screens
Move the $1,000 tag off the right cluster's heads — it overlaps character outlines and reads as clutter; float it higher with clear padding
The $1 badge slightly clips behind the SOLD signs — give the hero figure's price tag exclusive clearance space; it's the story anchor and currently competes
Raise the $1 tag's separation — its pale-blue chip blends into the mid-blue building behind it; add a drop shadow or darker outline so it reads at a glance
The moon and starfield in the top-left are near-invisible murk; either brighten them for depth or clean them out — half-lit background props read as noise
Warm the left character's rim light slightly toward the amber glow used on the right character so the two subjects feel lit by one source
Top ~40% of frame is a near-empty dark zone with only a faint moon — add subtle skyline texture, drifting particles, or push the crowd up to reclaim the dead zone
Cropped 'SOLD' tag on the far right edge (and left edge) reads as accidental cutoff — reposition tags fully inside the safe area or deliberately clip all of them symmetrically
The '$1' tag and the foreground figure both glow equally, splitting attention slightly — dim the SOLD labels and cool their glow so the $1 badge is the singular brightest element
The floating '$1' sign above the left character and the '$1' bill on the right read as two separate labels — unify with one consistent badge style or drop the bill's text to a pure icon
The upper third of the frame (sky) is a large dead zone — raise the characters slightly or add a subtle title/moon-weight element to fill the empty headroom
The faint white rain/marker specks near the top and bottom edges read as compression artifacts on small screens — either increase their contrast as intentional weather FX or remove them
Raise the bill/hand group slightly above vertical center to shrink the large empty sky dead zone occupying the top ~35% of frame
Add a subtle drop shadow or rim light behind the bill to separate it more cleanly from the dark building mass
Strengthen the moon glow behind the bill's upper edge so the eye path lands on the $1 immediately instead of wandering through the skyline
Kill one text system: the SOLD badges collide with the buyer's face and the header — keep the header + $1 tag, move SOLD badges below the character or drop them
Big dead zone between header banner and characters — raise characters or add midground detail (rain streaks, building glow) to bridge the top third
Boost legibility: outline or brighten the header text and SOLD labels; dark grey type on dark navy buildings will smear on a 6-inch daylight screen
Fill the large empty upper-third sky dead zone with a subtle moon glow, rain streaks emphasis, or a short hook text element to guide the eye downward
Differentiate the central character further (stronger rim light, color accent, or slight scale-up) so he reads instantly as the focal subject against the smiling crowd
Clarify the floating orange UI chips around the crowd — several are cropped or ambiguous shapes; either sharpen their meaning or reduce their count to cut peripheral clutter
